patients.summary: Retired administrative assistant with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and central diabetes insipidus who joined in 2019. Stage IA endometrial cancer treated surgically in 2020, later diabetic retinopathy, knee osteoarthritis, lisinopril angioedema, desmopressin-related hyponatremia and acute mitral regurgitation repaired surgically in 2025; records from outside care arrive unevenly.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56 y/o woman establishing care. Previous internist reducing hours.

Diabetes: type 2 since roughly 2006. Metformin 1000 twice a day, no other agents ever. Does not check sugars at home with any regularity. No lows. Last eye exam she can remember was well over a decade ago.

BP: on HCTZ 25 for years, tolerates it.

Diabetes insipidus (central): followed by an outside endocrinologist, on desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily. Says thirst and urination are well controlled on it. Sees endo about every 1-2 years.

PMH: as above, plus weight - she has carried extra weight since her 30s.
PSH: C-section 1988. Laparoscopic appendectomy 1995.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, HCTZ 25 mg daily, desmopressin 0.1 mg BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs -> rash.
FH: mother had endometrial cancer at 62. Father had type 2 diabetes with eye involvement. Sister with high blood pressure.
SH: retired administrative assistant. Has a grown daughter. Smoked about a pack a day for 20 years, stopped in 2005. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. No drugs.

ROS: negative except mild fatigue some afternoons.

Exam: BP 140/88. BMI 35. Pleasant, well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, healed lower transverse and laparoscopic scars. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament sensation normal both feet, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. T2DM - continue metformin. A1c, CMP, lipids, urine microalbumin today.
2. HTN - 140/88 today, a bit above goal. Continue HCTZ, recheck next visit.
3. Central DI - stable on desmopressin per endo; will watch sodium on our labs.
4. Obesity, BMI 35 - talked about small steps; she walks some.
5. Health maintenance - hep C and HIV screen today. Prior records requested for colonoscopy and mammogram dates. Flu shot and Shingrix next month at a nurse visit.
PHQ-2 0.

RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Donna, your labs are back. A1c 7.4, so diabetes is reasonably but not perfectly controlled. Kidney function, sodium and blood counts look fine. The urine protein screen was normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screening negative. Cholesterol numbers are in your chart. We'll go over everything at the January visit.

documents.body:

- Colonoscopy 2016: normal, repeat in 10 years.
- Screening mammogram February 2019: negative.
- Tdap 2014.
- Endocrinology letter dated March 2019: central diabetes insipidus, stable on desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily, sodium 140, follow up in 1 to 2 years.
- No prior eye exam reports in the packet.
Scanned to media. Health maintenance updated.

documents.title: Video visit - abnormal bleeding
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home, verified with name and DOB. In-person visits limited right now.

For the last half year her cycles have come anywhere from 3 to 6-7 weeks apart, and when they come the flow is heavy enough that she goes through a pad every hour or two. Then nothing at all for 2 months, and this past week some spotting. No pain. Some tiredness. No lightheadedness or fainting.

Given age 56, obesity, diabetes and her mother's endometrial cancer, this needs prompt gynecology evaluation with endometrial sampling. Urgent referral placed; gyn office will draw labs at the visit. Bleeding precautions reviewed - go to the ED for soaking more than a pad an hour for several hours or feeling faint.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - consultation letter
Date of visit: 04/27/2020

Thank you for sending Ms. Fairbanks, 56, for abnormal uterine bleeding.

History: About six months of unpredictable cycles (intervals 21 to 45 days) with heavy flow needing a pad change every one to two hours, then two months with no period, and a week of spotting before this visit. Type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Central diabetes insipidus. C-section 1988, laparoscopic appendectomy 1995. Medications metformin 1000 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily. Allergy: sulfa (rash). Mother with endometrial cancer at 62. Former smoker, quit 2005.

Exam: BP 142/90. BMI 35. External genitalia normal. Speculum: cervix without lesions, no discharge. Bimanual: uterus enlarged, non-tender; no adnexal masses.

Labs today: hemoglobin 10.2, platelets 250, fasting glucose 162, A1c 7.8.

Procedure: endometrial biopsy performed in the office without difficulty; sample sent to pathology.

Impression: perimenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding with risk factors for endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma. Will call her with pathology and plan.

Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of endometrium
conditions.note: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 1, on office biopsy

documents.title: Patient call - biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Donna called. Gynecology told her the biopsy showed endometrial cancer - per the result she read me from the portal, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 1. Gyn is sending her to gynecologic oncology; consult is set for later this month and surgery is being discussed. She is scared but practical; her mother went through the same thing. Answered questions about what grade 1 usually means. Offered a pre-op visit with us once a date is set. Added to problem list.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate in the 70s. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality. No prior tracing for comparison.

documents.title: Pre-operative evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op for laparoscopic hysterectomy with removal of tubes and ovaries and node mapping, planned 6/9 with gynecologic oncology.

Functional capacity: climbs two flights and does her own yard work without chest pain or breathlessness. No prior anesthesia problems (C-section, appendectomy). No bleeding disorder history.

Exam: Mask on. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes.
Labs: BMP and CBC drawn today; hemoglobin was 10.2 at gyn last month.

Assessment: low-risk patient for an intermediate-risk procedure; no further cardiac testing needed.
- Metformin: hold the morning of surgery, resume when eating.
- HCTZ: hold the morning of surgery.
- Desmopressin: continue; anesthesia should know about central DI and watch sodium and fluids peri-op. Letter faxed to surgeon.

reports.text:
Specimen: uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries; right and left pelvic sentinel lymph nodes; peritoneal washings.
Histologic type: endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
FIGO grade: 1.
Myometrial invasion: 30% of myometrial thickness.
Lymphovascular invasion: not identified.
Cervical stromal involvement: not identified.
Bilateral tubes and ovaries: no tumor.
Sentinel lymph nodes: right 0/1, left 0/1, negative including ultrastaging.
Peritoneal washings: negative for malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 1, invading less than half of the myometrium; nodes and washings negative. FIGO stage IA (pT1a pN0(sn)).

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology post-operative letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY
Re: Donna Fairbanks, DOB 07/29/1963

Dear colleague,
Ms. Fairbanks underwent total laparoscopic hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and sentinel lymph node mapping on 06/09/2020. She went home on post-operative day 1 and was seen in clinic two weeks later with well-healed port sites.

Final pathology is enclosed: endometrioid adenocarcinoma, grade 1, 30% myometrial invasion, no LVSI, sentinel nodes negative bilaterally, washings negative - FIGO stage IA. No adjuvant therapy is indicated.

Plan: surveillance visits with pelvic exam every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. She knows to report any vaginal bleeding.

Medications unchanged: metformin, hydrochlorothiazide, desmopressin. Allergy: sulfa (rash).

documents.title: Gyn onc records scanned

documents.title: Checking in after surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know the surgery went fine and I went home the next day. Saw the surgeon yesterday and she said I'm healing well and they got it all. Pathology was early stage and I don't need radiation. Sugars were a little high in the hospital but back to my usual now.

documents.title: RE: Checking in after surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news, Donna. Thanks for letting us know. We haven't received the paperwork yet and will ask the surgeon's office for it. Take it easy on lifting for the next few weeks. Let's see you in September for your physical.

documents.title: Annual physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
57 y/o here for physical, three months out from hysterectomy/BSO for stage IA endometrial cancer. Recovered well, no bleeding, no pelvic pain. Some hot flashes after the ovaries came out, tolerable. Gyn onc surveillance every 6 months.

Diabetes: home readings 150s-170s fasting. Admits eating has drifted with being home all the time this year. Metformin twice daily.
BP: home readings mostly 130s.
DI: unchanged on desmopressin.

Exam: BP measured, see vitals. Weight down a few pounds since last year. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, port scars healed. Ext no edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good. Skin no concerning lesions.

A/P
1. T2DM - A1c 8.4 today, up from 7.6 in January. Talked about adding a second medication; she would rather tighten up her eating and walking first now that she's recovered from surgery. Reasonable for a few months; recheck A1c in 3 months and add an agent if not improving.
2. HTN - continue HCTZ.
3. Endometrial cancer s/p surgery - surveillance with gyn onc.
4. Anemia before surgery (Hgb 10.2 at gyn) - CBC today now that the bleeding has stopped.
5. HM: flu shot today. Mammogram due - order placed. Colonoscopy 2016 normal. Shingrix complete. No Pap needed after hysterectomy. PHQ-2 1.
Follow-up 3 months for diabetes.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Comparison: 02/2019. The breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion. Skin and axillae unremarkable.

documents.title: Diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Last seen 9/2020; missed the December visit.

S: Vision in both eyes has been slowly getting blurrier for about a year and a half - harder to read the TV guide and street signs. No pain, no flashes or floaters, no double vision. Hasn't been to an eye doctor in more than 10 years. More thirsty than usual over the winter; says she let the diet go. Got her first COVID shot at the pharmacy, second one coming up.

O: BP 134/82. Weight down a bit. Alert, no focal neuro deficits. Fundi poorly seen undilated. Feet: monofilament intact.
Labs 3/30: A1c 11.7 (8.4 in Sept). Urine albumin/creatinine 64 - new microalbuminuria. Creatinine and sodium normal. Hgb 12.3.

A/P
1. T2DM, uncontrolled. Already on max metformin. Starting basal insulin: glargine 10 units at bedtime, raise 2 units every 3 days until fasting under 130, max 30 units without calling us. Pen teaching done by RN today, glucometer and supplies sent. Hypoglycemia rules reviewed.
2. Blurred vision, long-standing diabetes, no eye care in a decade - ophthalmology referral for dilated exam. Some of the blur may be glucose-related.
3. Microalbuminuria - recheck after sugars improve; will discuss kidney protection next visit.
4. HTN - acceptable today on HCTZ.
RN call in 2 weeks for doses. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY - consult letter
Exam date: 04/26/2021
Patient: Donna Fairbanks, 57

Reason for referral: slow loss of clarity in both eyes over roughly 18 months; type 2 diabetes; no eye examination in over ten years.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine at bedtime (recently started), hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily. Allergy: sulfa drugs (rash).
Recent labs per referring office: A1c 11.7%; urine positive for microalbumin.
BP 134/82.

Visual acuity (distance, current glasses): OD 20/40, OS 20/50.
Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. Motility full. Confrontation fields full. No focal neurologic deficit noted.
Intraocular pressures normal both eyes.
Anterior segment: clear corneas, deep quiet chambers, lenses clear.
Dilated fundus: scattered microaneurysms and a few dot-blot hemorrhages in both eyes; no venous beading, IRMA or neovascularization. Maculae flat without thickening or exudate on exam and OCT. Discs pink and sharp with healthy rims.

Assessment: mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes without macular edema. Reduced acuity is largely refractive; new spectacle prescription given.
Plan: improve glucose control gradually; repeat dilated exam in 12 months, sooner for any sudden change.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with mild nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema

Allergies: sulfa (rash).

documents.title: Follow-up: diabetes, albuminuria, knees
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing great with sugars. Glargine was down to 14 units because mornings were running 80s-90s. Has lost about 8 lb since fall. Wants to know if she can come off insulin.
New issue: both knees hurt for about 6 months - worse with stairs and long walks, better resting. Stiff for about 20 minutes on getting up. No swelling, redness, fever or injury.

O: BP 138/84. BMI 32. Knees: crepitus both, no effusion or warmth, full motion with end-range discomfort.
Labs 4/5: A1c 6.8. Urine albumin/creatinine 58 (64 last year) - persistent. Creatinine, potassium normal.

A/P
1. T2DM - stop glargine; metformin alone; recheck A1c in 5-6 months. Keep checking fasting a few times a week.
2. Microalbuminuria, persistent - start lisinopril 10 mg daily for kidney protection; BMP in 2 weeks. Continue HCTZ.
3. Bilateral knee pain with morning stiffness - most likely osteoarthritis, but given the stiffness she would like a rheumatology opinion; referral placed. Tylenol in the meantime.
4. Eye f/u due next month - she has it scheduled.

reports.text: Bilateral standing AP, lateral and sunrise views of both knees. Medial and patellofemoral joint space narrowing bilaterally with subchondral sclerosis and marginal osteophytes. No fracture, erosion or chondrocalcinosis. No joint effusion. Soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Degenerative changes of both knees consistent with osteoarthritis.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY - consultation
Visit date: 04/22/2022

58-year-old woman referred for knee pain. Background: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, central diabetes insipidus, endometrial cancer treated surgically in 2020, diabetic retinopathy followed by ophthalmology.

She describes half a year of pain in both knees brought on by activity and eased by rest, with roughly 20 minutes of stiffness after waking. No other joints involved, no rash, no constitutional symptoms.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide (her pressure is well controlled on it), metformin, lisinopril 10 mg recently added, desmopressin. Allergy: sulfa drugs (rash).

Exam: BMI 32. Knees without erythema or warmth. Bony enlargement of both knees with joint-line tenderness. No effusion. Range of motion preserved but uncomfortable at the extremes. Hands, wrists, shoulders and ankles normal.

Imaging today: joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes in both knees.

Impression: primary osteoarthritis of both knees. No features of inflammatory arthritis; no further serologic workup needed.

Recommendations: acetaminophen up to 1 g three times daily as needed; physical therapy for quadriceps strengthening; weight loss will help. Follow up here as needed.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth up to three times daily as needed for knee pain

documents.title: Rheumatology letter and next steps
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Donna, the rheumatologist's letter came in. It is osteoarthritis in both knees, not an inflammatory arthritis, which is good news. I've sent a physical therapy referral and added Tylenol to your list (up to 2 tablets three times a day as needed). Your kidney labs after starting lisinopril were fine - potassium and creatinine normal.

documents.title: Annual physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
59 y/o here for her yearly exam. No new concerns. Her daughter came along but had to head out partway through for her shift at work.

Interval: diabetes on metformin alone, home fasting mostly in the 120s. BP fine at home on lisinopril + HCTZ. Knees manageable since PT. Gyn onc says she is doing well, next check in June. DI unchanged on desmopressin.

Exam: Vitals within normal limits. BMI 31.
General: well appearing, somewhat nervous today.
Skin: mild velvety darkening at the back and sides of the neck (acanthosis nigricans). Otherwise clear.
HEENT, neck, thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Feet: monofilament and vibration normal, pulses intact.
Breasts: see below. Symmetric, no masses, skin or nipple changes, or axillary nodes either side.

Consent / understanding: when I explained the breast exam she became anxious and had a hard time following what I was describing. I slowed down, used plainer words, showed her on a diagram, and asked her to tell me back what we would do and why. She did so accurately, asked a sensible question about whether it would hurt, and agreed to the exam with the MA present. I'm satisfied she understood and was able to decide for herself - capacity for this decision intact. Documented as such.

A/P
1. T2DM with mild NPDR - labs today. Eye exam due next month.
2. HTN - at goal.
3. Microalbuminuria - urine ratio today.
4. Obesity - BMI 31, down from 35 when she joined. Problem list updated.
5. Hx endometrial cancer, stage IA, 2020 - no evidence of disease; surveillance continues with gyn onc. Problem list updated to history.
6. Acanthosis nigricans of the neck, mild - goes with insulin resistance; no treatment needed.
7. HM: mammogram 11/2022 negative. Colonoscopy 2016, due 2026. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Donna - A1c 7.3, about where it was in the fall. Kidney function and sodium normal, blood count normal. Urine protein ratio a little lower than last year, which is the direction we want. Cholesterol about the same. Nice job overall.

Plan: annual pelvic examination from here; she may alternate with her gynecologist. Any vaginal bleeding should prompt prompt evaluation.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED - physician record
Arrival 04/18/2024 09:40

CC: lips and tongue swollen.
HPI: 60-year-old woman who noticed puffy lips and a thick tongue on waking; it has steadily worsened over a few hours. No hives, no itching, no trouble breathing or swallowing, voice normal. No new foods, stings or medicines. History of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, central DI, endometrial cancer treated in 2020. Takes lisinopril, which she has been on for about two years, along with hydrochlorothiazide, metformin and desmopressin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 78, RR 16. Non-pitting swelling of upper and lower lips and tongue, no redness or warmth. Uvula midline and not swollen; floor of mouth soft; no stridor. Skin without urticaria. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.
Labs: Na 139, K 4.8, Cr 1.1. CBC within normal limits.

Course: methylprednisolone 125 mg IV, diphenhydramine 50 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV given once each. Observed six hours with serial airway checks; no progression, no airway intervention needed. Swelling clearly receding by discharge.

Impression: angioedema due to ACE inhibitor (lisinopril).
Disposition: home. Stop lisinopril permanently and avoid all ACE inhibitors. Return immediately for any throat tightness, voice change or trouble breathing. Follow up with PCP within a week.

documents.title: Went to the ER yesterday

documents.body: I woke up yesterday with my lips and tongue swollen up like a balloon and went to the ER. They gave me IV medicines and watched me most of the day. They said it was from the lisinopril and I should never take it again. Swelling is almost gone this morning. Do I still take the other pressure pill?

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm so sorry, that sounds frightening. Yes - stop the lisinopril for good, and keep taking the hydrochlorothiazide. I have marked lisinopril as a serious allergy in your chart so no one restarts it or a drug like it. If the swelling comes back or you have any trouble breathing or swallowing, call 911. Let's see you next week; the front desk will call with a time.

documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/19/2024, discharged 10/22/2024. Service: endocrinology.

Reason for admission: headache, nausea and confusion for two days.

History: 61-year-old woman with central diabetes insipidus, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and treated endometrial cancer. About ten days before admission her endocrinologist raised desmopressin from 0.1 mg to 0.2 mg twice daily because of ongoing thirst and frequent urination. Within days she developed headache and queasiness, and her daughter found her muddled and brought her in.
Home medications on admission: desmopressin 0.2 mg twice daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).

Admission exam: BP 130/85, HR 78. Oriented to self only. Mucous membranes moist. No peripheral edema. No focal deficits.
Labs: sodium 125, potassium 4.2, serum osmolality 260, urine osmolality 600, urine sodium 80.

Assessment: hypotonic euvolemic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine - SIADH physiology from excess antidiuretic effect after the desmopressin increase.

Course: desmopressin and hydrochlorothiazide held; fluid restriction to 1 L/day; sodium checked every 4-6 hours with a correction limit of 8 mEq/L per day. Sodium 129 the next morning and 133 on the day of discharge. Confusion cleared by hospital day 2; at discharge she was fully oriented and at her baseline per her daughter. Urine output increased as expected off desmopressin and desmopressin was restarted at the prior dose.

Discharge diagnoses: SIADH (desmopressin-related hyponatremia); central diabetes insipidus.
Discharge medications: desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily (back to prior dose); hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily resumed; metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with sodium; endocrinology in 2-3 months. Seek care for headache, vomiting or confusion.

We have no discharge paperwork - daughter will bring what she has; will request summary.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter after admission 10/19-10/22 for low sodium (125) with confusion. Per the discharge papers the daughter brought: endo had increased desmopressin to 0.2 mg twice daily about 10 days before; labs showed concentrated urine with low serum osm; treated as SIADH from the desmopressin with fluid restriction and holding the drug; discharged on 0.1 mg twice daily. Our med list never had the higher dose.

Now: thinking clearly, no headache or nausea. Thirst a bit more than ideal but she is tolerating it. Drinking to thirst, not forcing fluids.

Exam: alert and fully oriented, conversant, appropriate. Mucous membranes moist. No edema. Heart RRR.
Sodium drawn today; will send result by portal.

A/P
1. SIADH from desmopressin excess - resolved hyponatremia. Desmopressin 0.1 mg BID. Endo f/u being arranged; she should not change the dose without a sodium check. Added to problem list.
2. HTN - on HCTZ (resumed by hospital).
3. T2DM - A1c and urine ratio today.
Had flu and COVID shots at the pharmacy in September. Mammogram ordered.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (Cardiology / Cardiac Surgery)
Admitted 04/18/2025 via the ED to the cardiac ICU. Discharged 04/29/2025.

Presentation: about two hours into an afternoon of gardening she developed sudden, severe breathlessness, could not lie flat, and felt her heart racing. Background: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, central DI on desmopressin, endometrial cancer treated in 2020, desmopressin-related hyponatremia (SIADH) in 2024.
Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).

On arrival: RR 28, BP 150/90, HR 110. Crackles to the mid lung fields on both sides. A new holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla.
Troponin I <0.04; BNP 900; creatinine 1.1; BUN 18.
Chest film: pulmonary venous congestion with interstitial edema. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes.
Echo: severe mitral regurgitation from a flail posterior leaflet segment with ruptured chordae; LVEF 65%; LV not dilated.

Hospital course: IV furosemide and overnight bilevel positive airway pressure, with rapid improvement in breathing. Coronary angiography 04/20: no obstructive coronary artery disease. Cardiac surgery performed mitral valve repair on 04/22/2025 (resection of the flail posterior segment and annuloplasty ring). Uncomplicated recovery. Post-operative echo 04/26: trace residual MR, LVEF 60%. Sodium monitored closely given her DI; desmopressin continued at her usual dose with no hyponatremia.

Discharge diagnosis: acute severe mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture, status post mitral valve repair.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily (3 months after repair, cardiology to review); furosemide 20 mg daily for 2 weeks then stop; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily.
Follow-up: PCP in 1-2 weeks; cardiology and cardiac surgery clinic in 3 months with echo. Sternal precautions for 6 weeks.

documents.title: Gynecology visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY
Visit 04/23/2026

Ms. Fairbanks returns to us six years after her endometrial cancer was found here on biopsy; she had staging hysterectomy with BSO in 2020 (stage IA, grade 1) and has been followed since. For about three months she has noticed on-and-off vaginal bleeding, light. She had no bleeding at all from the 2020 surgery until this. No pelvic pain, no weight loss, no change in bowel habits.

Medications: metformin, hydrochlorothiazide, desmopressin. Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash). Family history: mother with endometrial cancer.

Exam: BP 132/86. BMI 31. Speculum: small amount of blood in the vaginal vault; cuff closed without a visible lesion. Bimanual: no palpable masses; no adnexal tenderness or masses.
Labs: hemoglobin 12.1, platelets 250, fasting glucose 146, creatinine 0.9.

Impression: postmenopausal bleeding after hysterectomy for endometrial cancer; recurrence at the vaginal cuff must be excluded.
Plan: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis; referred back to gynecologic oncology for examination and biopsy of the cuff.

documents.title: Bleeding again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted you to know I've had some spotting off and on since around January and saw the gynecologist yesterday. She wants a CT scan and a biopsy with the cancer doctor to make sure it's not back. I'm nervous. CT is May 7.

documents.title: RE: Bleeding again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Donna. Checking carefully is exactly the right step, and your cancer was found early and treated completely in 2020. Please have the gynecologist's office send us their note and any results. Call or message any time if you want to talk it through.

reports.text: Specimen: vaginal cuff, biopsy. Fragments of benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation. No dysplasia. No malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Vaginal cuff biopsy: benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation; negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology - cuff biopsy
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY
Visit 05/19/2026

Seen for intermittent vaginal bleeding six years after surgery for stage IA endometrioid endometrial cancer. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis on 05/07/2026 showed no evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.
Exam: no adenopathy. Abdomen benign. Speculum: cuff intact without a visible lesion; biopsies of the cuff taken. Rectovaginal exam without nodularity.
Pathology: benign squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation; no malignancy.
Impression: no evidence of recurrent endometrial cancer.
Plan: re-examine in 3 months, sooner if bleeding increases.
Allergies: lisinopril (angioedema), sulfa (rash).
